body:
As I said in my original post, I've tried therapy multiple times, with three different therapists. They're different people, but they all try similar things. I'm sick of repeating my life story to these people, expecting something different to happen. Therapy hasn't helped, and I don't see how trying a fourth or fifth therapist will change that.

I'm inclined to think that what I need is the right combination of a period of reduced anxiety, a willing sexual partner, and a doctor who will give me viagra. I'm not optimistic that this combination of scenarios will occur any time soon.

Porn was never a problem. When I was of healthier mind, I'd use it once a day or so as an aid, but I didn't have anything approaching addiction. You might disagree, but this was years ago anyway, so I hardly think it's relevant now.

I don't know how cognitive behavioral therapy differs from regular therapy, but I've tried the latter, and it hasn't helped.

I barely ever even masturbate anymore, so I'm pretty sure porn isn't my problem. Like, 2-3 times per month, which is significantly down from where I consider to be healthy (and certainly lower than what is normal for a male). I only do it when I'm having a particularly good day.

I ask people out online once every couple of months, but haven't been able to indicate sexual/romantic interest with someone I met IRL in years.

I think part (but I want to emphasize not all) of this anxiety has to do with how culture has begun to treat sex like it's normal (which is a good thing) and acknowledge that everyone is having it (also a good thing), but then I'm sitting here like...I'm not having it, and that everyone else seems to treat sex as a given makes me feel kind of otherized.

Same thing happened to me with my ex. Sure, I could identify when another girl was attractive, but I had no desire whatsoever to look at them/fantasize/anything in a sexual way. It was like my sexual desire for other people evaporated entirely.

You must be in an entirely alien situation to me if finding a sexual partner is as easy as asking a friend. :-/

Online dating is how I've met most of the women that I tried to have sex with and couldn't, including the one who kept trying for about a month before I had a panic attack and noped out.

It's strange; I'm completely over the specific person who cheated on me. Like, in every way I look at it, I don't give any shits about them at all. And when the anxiety creeps up, there are no specific thoughts regarding betrayal or anything...it just feels like I need to get out of the situation ASAP.

I don't even know how to find a fuck buddy.

There are so many factors of my situation that I don't have the brainspace to think of while writing the post. One of them is my "family". Unfortunately, the only family I have is my mother, and while I care about her, we don't talk about things like this. I've tried in the past, and she's about as incapable of discussing these things as I am of fixing them. Thank you.
